when: Uncovers the latent factor structure of a set of items when the structure is not specified in advance.
example: You have twenty attitude questions and do not yet know how they group. Exploratory factor analysis looks for a smaller set of hidden themes that explain the answers.
small_sample: Factor analysis needs many cases per item, so it is fragile in small samples. Use parallel analysis to decide the number of factors, and treat a small-sample solution as exploratory only.
assumptions: Items are continuous or treated as ordinal with an appropriate correlation matrix
Sampling adequacy is acceptable (KMO above .60) and Bartlett's test is significant
Sample size is adequate, commonly 5 to 10 cases per item
alternative: Confirmatory factor analysis, when theory specifies the structure in advance

survey_skeleton:
# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "efa_solution").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
agree5 <- sf_choices("agree5", 1:5,
  c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: The item pool to explore ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: The item pool to explore", type = "section_break")
scale_1_1 <- sf_item("scale_1_1", "[Item pool item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "scale_1")
scale_1_2 <- sf_item("scale_1_2", "[Item pool item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "scale_1")
scale_1_3 <- sf_item("scale_1_3", "[Item pool item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "scale_1")
scale_1_4 <- sf_item("scale_1_4", "[Item pool item 4 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "scale_1")
scale_1_5 <- sf_item("scale_1_5", "[Item pool item 5 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "scale_1")
scale_1_6 <- sf_item("scale_1_6", "[Item pool item 6 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "scale_1")
scale_1 <- sf_scale("scale_1", "Item pool", c("scale_1_1", "scale_1_2", "scale_1_3", "scale_1_4", "scale_1_5", "scale_1_6"), method = "mean")

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, scale_1_1, scale_1_2, scale_1_3, scale_1_4, scale_1_5, scale_1_6, scale_1
  )
)

# Check readiness, then extract (read responses first):
# responses <- read_responses("my_data.csv", instr, strict = FALSE)
efa_report(responses, instr)
efa_solution(responses, instr)
